cd ~/your-project
pi
# Inside Pi, run /login, then give it a small task.

install-omp.code:
curl -fsSL https://omp.sh/install -o omp-install.sh
less omp-install.sh
sh omp-install.sh --binary
omp --version

setup.code:
mkdir openharness && cd openharness
git init -q
mkdir -p src/features extensions bin skills/engineering-loop prompts test
printf 'node_modules/\n.openharness/\n' > .gitignore

skill.code:
---
name: engineering-loop
description: How to work inside OpenHarness. Use for any change to this codebase that will go through verification and review.
---

# The engineering loop

1. Read before you write. Use `read_lines`, because its anchors are how you edit.
2. Make the smallest change that solves the task.
3. Run the project's checks yourself before you say you are done.
4. Stop when you are done. The harness runs `verify` and review when you finish, and it will send you back with the reason if either fails.
5. If you are sent back, fix the cause. Never edit a test only to make it pass.
6. Split work that has independent parts with `delegate`, then merge each branch it returns.

ship.code:
---
description: Take a task from plan to a reviewed change
argument-hint: "<task>"
---
Use the engineering-loop skill. Task: $@

Make the change, get the checks green, and finish with a short summary of what changed and why.

try-it-in.code:
/plan add input validation to the signup form
/ship fix the failing date test
/report

link.code:
npm link
cd ~/your-project
openharness init
openharness run "fix the failing date test"
echo "exit code: $?"
openharness report
